title: Supported Source Formats
summary: Every document, data, video, audio, and image format Papyrus can open, with full feature parity.
body:
# Supported Source Formats

Papyrus can open many kinds of sources beyond PDF. Every format below supports the same core features: highlighting, notes, AI analysis (Analysis tab, Chat, Custom Tools), universal search, and jump-to-source (clicking a citation, note, or search result navigates back to the exact spot in the original file).

## Documents

| Format | Extension | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PDF | .pdf | Full support — pages, highlighting, OCR for scanned pages |
| Word | .docx | Headings and tables are recognised as document structure |
| Legacy Word | .doc | Requires LibreOffice installed on your system — see below |
| EPUB | .epub | Chapters and headings are recognised |
| Plain Text | .txt | — |
| Markdown | .md | `#`/`##` headings are recognised |
| HTML | .html, .htm | Headings and paragraphs are recognised |
| Rich Text | .rtf | — |

These all open in a shared read-only text viewer with zoom and fuzzy jump-to-source search.

## Data files

| Format | Extension | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| CSV / TSV | .csv, .tsv | Opens as a read-only preview; use **Open in Data Dock** to edit |
| Excel Workbook | .xlsx | Same dual-mode as CSV; only the active sheet is loaded |

See the **CSV/Excel: Preview vs. Edit** help topic for details on the dual-mode behaviour.

## Video & audio

| Format | Extensions |
|---|---|
| Video | .mp4, .mov, .mkv, .webm, .avi, .m4v, .wmv, .flv, .mpg, .mpeg, .3gp, .ogv, .ts |
| Audio | .mp3, .wav, .m4a, .flac, .ogg, .aac, .wma, .opus |

Both are automatically transcribed in the background using the same offline speech-to-text engine, giving you searchable captions and timestamp-accurate jump-to-source for both.

## Images

Standalone images (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .tiff, .bmp, .webp) are OCR'd automatically, giving you the same word-level highlighting and jump-to-source as a scanned PDF page.

## Legacy .doc caveat

The old binary `.doc` format has no reliable pure-Python reader. Papyrus converts it using LibreOffice if it is installed on your system (checks for the `soffice` command). If LibreOffice is not found, `.doc` files show as unavailable with an explanation — install LibreOffice (free) to enable them, or re-save the file as `.docx` from Word.

## For plugin authors

Plugins can register entirely new source formats — see the Plugin API documentation for `api.source_formats.register()`, `api.gui_extensions.add_source_viewer()`, and `api.gui_extensions.add_citation_source_handler()`.

title: CSV/Excel: Preview vs. Edit
summary: CSV/TSV/Excel files open read-only by default; one button promotes them to an editable Data Dock dataset.
body:
# CSV/Excel: Preview vs. Edit

When you open a `.csv`, `.tsv`, or `.xlsx` file from the Document Explorer, it opens like any other source — as a read-only table preview in the main viewer area. This keeps the file's on-disk data untouched until you explicitly choose to edit it.

## Opening the editable version

Click **Open in Data Dock** in the preview's toolbar. This loads the same parsed data into the Data Dock, where you can:

- Edit individual cells
- Add computed columns (sum, average)
- Generate charts
- Export the result

The preview and the Data Dock both parse the file the same way, so what you see in the preview is exactly what you'll get when you open it for editing.

## Why read-only by default?

Separating viewing from editing means casually opening a data file (e.g. to check a citation or read a value) never risks accidentally modifying it. You only get an editable copy when you ask for one.

## Excel workbooks

Only the active (first) sheet of an `.xlsx` file is loaded. Multi-sheet support is planned for a future release — for now, split additional sheets into separate files if you need to work with them.

title: Grounded Intelligence and Analysis Graphs
summary: Run fast artifact-first analysis, understand graph quality, and inspect exact source evidence.
body:
# Grounded Intelligence and Analysis Graphs

Papyrus builds a source-backed baseline before model synthesis. Classifier roles describe individual passages: a passage labelled reasoning or counterclaim does not, by itself, establish which other passage it supports or contradicts.

## Run an analysis

1. Open Research → Analysis and select a mode and sources.
2. Enter a specific topic to narrow the analysis. Current focus filtering matches topical words in passage text and can include one hop of a reviewed semantic connection with scoped evidence. Headings and retrieval scores cannot make an unrelated passage eligible. This conservative filter can miss paraphrases and does not yet implement Boolean research expressions.
3. Choose a detail profile. Counts are targets when relevant material exists, not quotas the application fills with invented connections.
4. Run Analysis. An empty focused result means the selected evidence did not meet the focus filter; broaden or reword the topic if appropriate.

## Partial results and suggestions

A baseline can contain useful quotations and propositions without enough established connections. The card marks this **Partial analysis** and separates semantic links from source/grouping links. A source quotation link identifies provenance; it does not establish support. Requested coverage thresholds are not lowered to make a sparse source pass.

The optional model pass may propose up to three label/statement changes and twelve relations over existing node IDs. A relation needs supplied evidence aliases, valid endpoint types and a specific explanation. New connections remain **unreviewed suggestions**, even when they pass those checks. Typed references and lexical overlap do not prove semantic correctness. Review suggested connections in the workspace before relying on them.

Model patches preserve IDs, canonical quotations, existing links and reviewed edits. Invalid changes are rejected. One authorized repair can be attempted; an empty, deliberate abstention does not trigger another call. If a source changes while the model runs, stale nodes are removed and the analysis needs refreshing. A failed model proposal falls back to current grounded material with diagnostics, not an invented hierarchy.

## Evidence provenance and workspace import

Evidence text comes from the canonical artifact, not a model-authored quotation. References retain artifact IDs and locators. Both workspace import paths normalize inverse relation directions: A supported by B becomes B supports A. Suggested versus reviewed relation state is retained. Workspace copies are independently editable.

## Caching and current limitations

Unchanged runs use a scoped cache. Changes to source intelligence, prompts, contracts, focus, model or detail invalidate affected results. Older cached graphs with heuristic support links are invalidated by the analysis contract update.

Template projection compilation, complete custom-mode prerequisites, exact serialized provider context budgets and real small-model quality/latency qualification remain Phase 8 work. Current patches do not automatically reclassify a claim as support or contradiction for a tracked proposition. Existing prompts remain editable in Prompt Editor; versioned v5 analysis prompts describe the new bounded patch contract.


## Compiled templates and readiness

Built-in, saved, plugin and runtime contracts now use one live-registry compiler. Template selections replace the default vocabulary. Numeric/Boolean bounds and registered endpoint/renderer compatibility are checked; impossible node limits fail rather than being silently enlarged. Run and cache lookup use the same resolved contract, source scope and prerequisite groups. Caller-supplied internal budgets or cache hashes cannot replace this resolved state.

The analysis picker reports invalid saved modes while keeping valid modes available. Contract/readiness checks and dispatch run in a worker. Required processing adapts to source category through the shared processing planner, then current artifacts are checked before inference. Explicit empty preparation does not trigger a hidden full ingestion. Older artifact-type lists retain their documented any-across-selection compatibility behavior; new contracts can specify all/any and per-source requirements.

This checkpoint supports canonical argument-unit projection and an independent user-focus root. Valid registered types without a source projection remain unmapped; the compiler does not create method-step/person/timeline nodes or infer stance merely because a template requests them. Exact serialized context budgets, semantic projection providers and live-model recovery/quality acceptance remain Phase 8 work.


## Model context and source integrity

New graph analyses send complete evidence groups: each displayed model node travels with all of its selected quotation references. Oversized groups are omitted whole; source quotations and aliases are not cut to fit. The result card shows how many groups reached the model. Material omitted from the model request remains in the current local baseline. Only nodes and quotation aliases actually supplied in that attempt can authorize model suggestions. Synthesis and repair have separate receipts.

Prompt Trace shows the final request and the artifact IDs actually supplied. System/Query v6 and Repair v4 remain editable in Prompt Editor. Source text containing braces or placeholder-shaped expressions is passed as source data and preserved through saving.

Packing currently uses a conservative text estimate with system/schema/output reserves, not exact provider token accounting. Very small contexts may not fit the fixed instructions at all and will be refused. Exact provider limits, live failure recovery and local-model quality qualification remain under development. Existing saved workflows using inline context retain their compatibility behavior.

title: Reviewing Intelligence Artifacts
summary: Browse dates, citations, and argument roles; correct artifacts without losing source history.
body:
# Review intelligence artifacts

Open the Intelligence dock and choose a source or the whole project. The Timeline shows contextual date mentions and excludes reference years, publication metadata, copyright notices and years used in instrument names. These observations remain inspectable in the artifact list, with a context role and an exclusion reason. Docket, section, page and quantity numbers are not dates. A date without a normalized value remains marked unresolved; ordinary claims are not added as undated timeline events. After an update, use Run missing or rerun Dates and Citations to rebuild older observations. Claims & Evidence shows each argument unit's current role and confidence. Citations groups each bibliography entry with its in-text references, and unmatched references appear separately.

Select an item to inspect its labeled fields. Use **Jump to source** to open the item's own source at its recorded location; the status line under the tabs says how exact that location is (see *Jumping to an artifact's source*). Choose **Correct** to edit text, a classification, a date, or another typed field. To reassign an in-text reference, choose its bibliography entry in the same dialog. Source location and origin fields remain locked until you explicitly confirm that the current provenance is wrong. Record IDs and revision timestamps are maintained by the app.

Use **History** to compare human revisions with later machine results. Rerunning a stage preserves reviewed corrections and shows competing machine output as a proposal. If a tab is empty, follow its next-step message to run the required stage. You can sort table columns and use the search box to narrow what is shown. Raw JSON is available through the advanced toggle in the inspector.

## Method and model

The inspector's **Method** line says how each item was made: deterministic rules, the heuristic scorer, a learned model (with its name and version), the assistant, or you. *No model used* means rules or heuristics produced it — not missing data. Items created before methods were recorded say so until their stage is rerun.

## When processing changes an item

**History** now also shows changes made by reprocessing (labelled *machine:* plus the producer). If a rebuild gives an item a new identity, your review, corrections and citation assignment move to the matching new item automatically. If several new items could match, the old item stays visible with a *migration conflict* note listing the candidates, so you can re-apply the decision rather than lose it.

## Notes

A note on a highlight is stored separately from the quoted passage and records who wrote it — you, or an assistant suggestion you saved. Notes are never treated as source text. Deleting the highlight retires its note.

## Citation uncertainty

Grouped numeric references can be partly matched: **Missing references: 99** means another part resolved but reference 99 did not. Same-author/year candidates without a distinguishing suffix remain **Ambiguous — review assignment**, with candidate IDs retained for inspection. They are not assigned automatically. Full legal references and supported short forms use recorded source spans; an Id. chain only resolves when one nearby antecedent is known. Unsupported or uncertain references remain unmatched. Manual assignments survive reruns. The source dropdown updates when documents are added, renamed or removed while the dock is open.

title: Jumping to an Artifact's Source
summary: How Jump to source finds the exact occurrence, and what Exact, Repaired, Approximate and Unavailable mean.
body:
# Jumping to an artifact's source

Select an item in the Intelligence dock and choose **Jump to source** (bindable as *Jump to Artifact Source* in Settings → Shortcuts). Papyrus opens the source the item was extracted from — identified by its project ID, never by matching a file name — and highlights the recorded occurrence. The search bar is not used, so a phrase that repeats on the same page, or two files with the same name, cannot send you to the wrong place.

## Location precision

The status line under the tabs reports what was achieved:

- **Exact location highlighted** — the extractor recorded character offsets, they still match the source text, and the highlight covers exactly those characters.
- **Location repaired** — offsets were missing (for example on items extracted before this version, or items you reviewed before it) or no longer matched, but the item's text occurs once inside its recorded block. When the phrase repeats inside that block, the occurrence closest to the old offset is chosen.
- **Approximate location** — only the block or page is known, or the page geometry no longer reproduces the stored text. The whole block is highlighted rather than guessing a word.
- **Source unavailable** / **No source location recorded** — the source was removed, its file is missing, or the item has no location. Nothing is opened.

Video and audio items seek to their transcript segment's start time; this is segment-level, not word-level. Your own highlights jump to their saved region.

## Chat citations, notes and search results

Jumps from chat citation bubbles, the Notes dock, search results and the RAG context viewer first try to place the quoted text in exactly one recorded passage of the named source (an exact file name; when two files share a name, the one containing the quote wins). If that succeeds the passage is highlighted the same way; if the quote appears in several passages or none, Papyrus falls back to the older text search.

## When the file changed

Every item records which version of the source file it was extracted from. If the file has changed since, an otherwise exact jump is reported as **Location repaired** with a note to rerun processing.

## Improving precision

Rerun the **Dates** or **Citations** stage for a source to record character offsets on items extracted by older versions. Reviewed items keep your corrections; their location is repaired from the recorded block instead.

title: Processing Plans, Stage Outcomes and Sentence Roles
summary: What each processing stage does, why it runs, what blocked/cancelled mean, and how argument roles are labelled.
body:
# Processing plans and outcomes

When you add sources, the processing dialog lists every stage from the live registry and previews, for each kind of source in the batch (documents, data files, audio/video), which stages will run and why: chosen by the **preset**, by **your override**, or **required by** another stage. The same plan is what the background queue executes.

## Stage outcomes

- **complete** — ran successfully; zero results is valid (a document without dates).
- **blocked** — waiting for a prerequisite: OCR for a scanned PDF (see *Why Intelligence Asks for OCR*), a transcript that has not been made yet, an unfinished earlier stage, a missing loader or embedding model. It runs once the prerequisite exists.
- **cancelled** — stopped by you, by removing the source, or by closing the project.
- **failed** — an error occurred; the run history shows it.
- **stale** — inputs, the relevant settings, or the model changed since it last ran. Unrelated setting changes do not make stages stale.

Repeated requests for the same stage are merged into one job. Closing a project cancels its work and discards late results, so nothing is written into the next project.

## Data files

CSV, TSV and Excel files are loaded into a table artifact plus one searchable artifact per row ("Column: value; …"), indexed for keyword and semantic search.

## Audio and video

**Index transcript** indexes an existing transcript; it does not transcribe. Until transcription finishes, dependent stages show *blocked: waiting for transcription*.

## Sentence (argument) roles

The built-in rules retain every canonical source sentence, but publish an argument unit only when there is a supported role. Headings, citation-only lines, incomplete fragments and ordinary background remain searchable without becoming argument nodes. Roles are claim, evidence, reasoning, methodology, counterclaim and limitation; contrast words or a citation year alone do not establish a role. A rule confidence is an interpretable strength, not a measured probability of correctness.

In **Settings → AI Setup → Pipeline Models**, the optional **sentence-role enhancer** (about 95 MB, CPU only) tests editable role/background hypotheses on uncertain eligible prose. It requires entailment and separation, may abstain, and never promotes unsupported domain roles. Legal restrictions are not automatically research limitations. You can switch it off per project. Current local PDF tests did not show a role-quality gain from larger NLI encoders; a model being larger does not establish that it is suitable for this task.

Custom task-trained ONNX imports require model.onnx, tokenizer.json and a unique supported labels.json mapping. Invalid mappings/output shapes or nonfinite scores fall back to rules with a reason; uncertain probabilities/margins can stay unknown. Each argument unit shows the actual method/model identity. Model or hypothesis changes mark the affected stage for rerun. Select **Run missing** after an upgrade to rebuild stale sections, citations and roles. Corrections are retained; a reviewed occurrence that cannot safely migrate after new segmentation is flagged for review.

title: Understanding and reviewing intelligence artifacts
summary: Artifacts are reusable, source-linked observations and authored notes.
body:
Artifacts are reusable, source-linked observations and authored notes. Select a record in Intelligence, resize the divider and edit its permitted semantic fields inline. Save publishes a human correction; Verify confirms the record; Reject hides it from current retrieval. Undo creates an audit revision and is blocked after a newer edit. Source quotes, identity, producer/model data and lifecycle state are protected. Repair source location requires explicit confirmation. Raw JSON is an advanced, read-only view. Review issues cycles through uncertain records, unknown argument roles, citation matches, dates, entity categories and migration conflicts. Skip/Defer progress and the last undo receipt are saved with the project. Revisit skipped clears those exclusions. No model is retrained or similar artifacts automatically relabelled by this workflow.

Artifact types: source identifies an imported source; block preserves parsed text/layout; section groups document structure; sentence is a bounded passage; transcript_segment is timed speech; entity is a project-level canonical identity and entity_mention is an exact occurrence; date_mention is a temporal observation; citation_entry is a bibliography authority and in_text_citation is a reference occurrence; table/table_row and figure preserve structured content; annotation/note are authored research content; argument_unit assigns a role to a source passage; summary compresses source content; analysis_result/analysis_answer record derived analysis. Other/plugin types remain inspectable through their registered source adapters.

An event timeline, Boolean entity filters, automatic networks and feedback propagation are separate planned capabilities. The current timeline displays eligible date observations.

## Complete browsing and expanded editing

Use **Expand inspector** for the shared editor in a larger window. Select an entity or bibliography entry and choose **Browse all occurrences** to move beyond the bounded child preview. **Runs** now pages and searches the full history. The project saves browsing preferences; see **Browsing intelligence and processing history** for scope, sorting and cursor behavior.

title: Artifact field: exact text
summary: The recorded source passage, preserving the evidence text.

title: Artifact field: normalized text

title: Artifact field: confidence
summary: A score from the recorded method, or an explicit human assessment after review.
body: A score from the recorded method, or an explicit human assessment after review. Scores from different models/rules are not interchangeable calibrated probabilities. title: Artifact field: bibliography match
summary: The active bibliography authority assigned to an in-text reference.
body: The active bibliography authority assigned to an in-text reference. Choose an entry from the same source. Search by title/author/reference text and press Enter to find entries beyond the first page. Unmatched is an explicit valid decision. Reassignment is recorded and can be undone.

title: Artifact field: review state
summary: Unreviewed is machine output awaiting review; verified confirms it; corrected records a human change; rejected excludes it from current retrieval; superseded marks replaced data.
body: Unreviewed is machine output awaiting review; verified confirms it; corrected records a human change; rejected excludes it from current retrieval; superseded marks replaced data. Use explicit Verify/Reject/Save commands, not a free-text status editor.

title: Artifact field: status
summary: A processing lifecycle field such as complete, stale, archived or superseded.
body: A processing lifecycle field such as complete, stale, archived or superseded. It is managed by processing; review actions do not falsely mark a failed/stale stage complete.

title: Artifact field: metadata
summary: Recorded extraction/context information.
body: Recorded extraction/context information. Only explicitly defined semantic fields are editable. Scores, offsets, coverage diagnostics, producer identity and derivation data remain read-only. Plugin-specific meanings can be documented through the Help Registry.

title: Artifact field: locator
summary: The recorded source coordinates: PDF page/block/character span, media time/segment, or another adapter location.
body: The recorded source coordinates: PDF page/block/character span, media time/segment, or another adapter location. Jump to source resolves this anchor off-thread and reports exact/repaired/coarse precision. Confirm the current location is wrong before repairing coordinates.

title: Artifact field: source path
summary: The registered source path, read-only in ordinary review.
body: The registered source path, read-only in ordinary review. It is not a filename search hint; navigation resolves the source identity and recorded anchor.

title: Artifact field: source type
summary: The registered format/adapter of the source.
body: The registered format/adapter of the source. It is read-only and determines the valid navigation coordinates.

title: Artifact field: section path
summary: The recorded section hierarchy.
body: The recorded section hierarchy. It provides context and retrieval coverage, and is derived from source structure.

title: Artifact field: source id
summary: The stable project identity of the source; it is not a display name.
body: The stable project identity of the source; it is not a display name. Read-only and preserved for source-safe navigation.

title: Artifact field: artifact id
summary: The stable identity of this artifact, shared by RAG, notes, graphs and plugins.
body: The stable identity of this artifact, shared by RAG, notes, graphs and plugins. It is read-only and remains stable across human revisions.

title: Artifact field: revision
summary: The current audit revision.
body: The current audit revision. Saves and undo create history; stale editors cannot overwrite a newer revision.

title: Artifact field: created at
summary: The recorded creation time.
body: The recorded creation time. It is managed by the backend and does not describe an event mentioned in the document.

title: Artifact field: updated at
summary: The time the current projection last changed.
body: The time the current projection last changed. It supports cursor invalidation and audit history, not event timelines.

title: Artifact field: method
summary: The actual producer, version, backend and model/fallback that created the artifact.
body: The actual producer, version, backend and model/fallback that created the artifact. Built-in deterministic rules may use no model; review does not rewrite this identity.

title: Artifact field: model name
summary: The actual recorded model, none for model-free work, or unknown when the originating model was not recorded.
body: The actual recorded model, none for model-free work, or unknown when the originating learned/generative model was not recorded unambiguously. Unknown is not evidence that no model was used. An assistant note uses its originating trace, never the currently selected model. Installing a classifier or changing models does not rewrite old provenance. This field is immutable in ordinary review.

title: Artifact field: extractor name
summary: The method that extracted this record.
body: The method that extracted this record. It is producer-owned and read-only.

summary: The recorded extraction method version, used for processing freshness.
body: The recorded extraction method version, used for processing freshness. It is read-only.

summary: The recorded page coordinate used by the source adapter.
body: The recorded page coordinate used by the source adapter. Jump to source verifies it against the stored span; repair only after checking the original passage.

summary: The recorded page coordinate; it is source-adapter data and not a timeline date.
body: The recorded page coordinate; it is source-adapter data and not a timeline date.

summary: The recorded beginning of a source span, usually relative to raw block text.
body: The recorded beginning of a source span, usually relative to raw block text. It is not an offset into reformatted display text.

summary: The recorded end of a source span.

summary: The beginning coordinate/time of a source occurrence, interpreted by its adapter.
body: The beginning coordinate/time of a source occurrence, interpreted by its adapter. Media values are seconds; block spans retain their coordinate basis.

summary: The ending coordinate/time of a source occurrence.
body: The ending coordinate/time of a source occurrence. It must not precede its start.

title: Artifact field: producer
