title: Browsing intelligence and processing history
summary: Save layouts, expand the editor, and browse complete occurrence and run lists.
body:
# Browsing intelligence

Choose a source or Whole project, then a view. Search runs across all matching records, including records beyond the current page. Previous page and Next page navigate bounded pages; a changed artifact or processing run invalidates the corresponding cursor and restarts the view instead of mixing revisions.

## Saved layout

The project remembers the selected view, source, search, per-view splitter sizes, expanded entity/bibliography rows and optional page sorting. It saves these preferences in the background. Reopening the dock restores them. If the remembered source is unavailable, the scope shows Whole project. Different projects retain their own preferences. Page cursors and unsaved edits are not restored.

## Sorting and filters

Most tabs have a filter row under their buttons. **Sort** orders the whole result, not just the page: Most or Least mentioned, Name A–Z or Z–A, Recently updated, or Most confident, depending on the tab. **Types** (People & Places, Explore), **Kinds** (Explore, Notes, Contents, Citations), **Roles** (Claims & Evidence) and **Review** are menus with one tick box per value and its count in the current scope; nothing ticked means no restriction, and **Show all** clears the menu. People & Places starts with *Hide dates, numbers and measures* ticked, so the list shows names; untick it to see them. The search box searches the current tab across all pages. Each tab remembers its sort and filters in this project.

## Tags

**Tags** filters by the tags on the records themselves (add them in Your review); tick several to see any of them, or turn on **Require all ticked tags** to narrow. **Document tags** shows only what comes from documents carrying a project tag (tag documents in the document list); entities count where they are mentioned. Both work together with the search box, sort and the other menus.

## Explore

Explore searches everything the system extracted. Set Kinds to Entity to list entities with mention counts and sort by mentions; search a name such as “Spain”, select the spellings that are the same place and use **Merge selected**. Two selected entities open the reviewed decision window; three or more are merged into the most mentioned one as a single decision after you confirm, and **Undo merge** reverses all of it.

## Buttons

Intelligence buttons show a single symbol; hover one to see its full name and what it does (keyboard and screen readers use the full name). Common symbols: ✔ verify or confirm, ✖ reject, ↶ undo, 💾 save, ↗ go to the source, ⇉ merge, ≠ keep separate, ⊂ group under, ✂ split, 🔗 connections, ⚑ review issues, ⚙ processing, ⟳ refresh, ⚡ run missing, ◀ ▶ pages, ? help.

## Mentions in context

Any entity shown in an inspector (the dock, Review issues, or a merge/grouping decision) has **All mentions** under it: expand it to list every mention with its page and sentence, select one and press ↗ (or double-click) to open the source at that exact mention.

Select any mention (expand an entity in People & Places or Explore, or in Browse all occurrences) and the inspector shows the whole sentence it is in, with the mention in bold and its page, so you can judge it without jumping to the source.

## Column sorting

Clicking a column header sorts the current page only; the header tooltip states this. This local sorting preference is saved. Use **Reset view layout** to restore backend order, the default splitter and collapsed rows. Search and source filters still cover the full scope.

## Expand the inspector

Select a record and use Expand inspector to open the same editor in a resizable, modeless window. Save, Verify, Reject and Undo follow the same typed rules and revision checks as the dock. Source quotes and producer identity remain read-only. Save or discard pending edits before selecting a different record in that window. Jump to source uses its recorded anchor.

## Browse all occurrences

Select an entity parent or bibliography entry, then Browse all occurrences. The dock's children are bounded previews; this separate browser shows every current occurrence in 100-record pages. Entity mentions respect the selected source scope. Bibliography references use the same effective match as the dock, including a human reassignment, and are restricted to the entry's source. Search covers all occurrences. Select a passage to inspect/edit it with the shared controls or jump to its exact recorded location. Rejected and superseded occurrences are excluded.

## Processing history

Runs contains processing records, not source artifacts. It pages beyond 1,000 runs and searches stages, outcomes, methods, models and diagnostic text. Select a run for timing, recorded method/model and output count. Run IDs, recorded outcomes and outputs are read-only. Rerun stage queues a new run; it does not rewrite the old record. The Overview's run counts cover the full selected scope.

## What is still being built

Processing… opens the per-source processing/readiness and model-install panel. Review issues now includes relation assertions and changed-source resolution; entity grouping uses the same decision panel. This browsing delivery does not add automatic classifier training, event timelines or inferred relationship confirmation.

## Notes, citations and revision history

Notes and history show up to 25 records per page and one selected detail. Drag the divider to give the detail more room. Arrow keys change selection; a short pause avoids rebuilding details while you move quickly. The old detail is disabled until the new one is ready. Previous/Next reaches all records, including machine proposals beyond the first page. Back to current artifact returns from history to the editor. Historical snapshots are read-only; advanced JSON shows the selected record only.

A response with many citations uses the same paged browser and one note bubble. Unsaved commentary stays with each citation while you browse; it becomes a project note only when explicitly saved.

## Saved chat pages

Reopened chat loads up to 12 saved records at a time. Older messages and Newer messages navigate history without duplicating saved messages. Ordinary question/response groups stay together where possible. A response longer than one page is marked Continued response; its beginning is on an older page. Finish a live response before changing pages.

## Text, book and image views

Book and normal text mode use the same cached extraction. Large text is paged; Next/Previous reaches later text and recorded anchors open the correct page directly. Select within a loaded page to save a verified note. Process an old or missing extraction first. PDF book text cannot supply PDF word geometry: switch to PDF view to annotate it. Images decode in the background at a bounded display size; saved OCR regions retain original image pixel coordinates.

title: Source processing and model readiness
summary: Choose a source plan, run missing or stale stages, inspect prerequisites and manage local models.
body:
# Source processing and model readiness

Open Intelligence → Processing… and choose a source. This resizable window uses the same processing policy, stage registry and producers as ingestion. The table distinguishes last outcomes from readiness now. Select a row to read its purpose, cost, prerequisites, errors, method that would run now and method recorded on the last run. Historical runs without an identity are labelled explicitly.

## Choose a plan

Pick a preset and check stages. Required prerequisites remain checked even if you try to disable them while keeping a dependent stage. Changes are drafts until Save source plan; Discard draft reloads the saved policy. Save before running or switching sources. Saving a plan does not run processing. Unsupported, disabled and generative stages cannot be selected for local processing. The saved plan applies to this source; defaults for future imports remain in Settings.

## Run more processing

Run missing processes selected stages whose successful fingerprints are not current, including failed or blocked work; completed current inputs are reused. Rerun stale runs only selected stages marked stale, with prerequisites. Run selected stage prepares the highlighted stage if needed. Force rerun stage reruns that stage even when current, reusing current prerequisites; downstream artifacts become stale when upstream work is refreshed. A fresh successful stage with zero outputs remains current. Force rerun is the way to test persistence of corrections when no stages are stale; human reviews follow the existing migration/proposal rules.

These commands run through the registered source-processing workflow in the process monitor. Cancel this run targets only this panel's request, including requests still queued, and requests cooperative cancellation at producer boundaries. Closing the window leaves a processing run in the monitor; clearing the project requests cancellation and closes the window. A completed workflow can contain blocked or failed stages: inspect its summary and outcomes.

## Models and fallback

Selected stage details list its declared catalog models, installation status, task, hardware guidance, licensing and evaluation limits. Optional models can be missing while built-in deterministic or heuristic methods remain usable. A heuristic has model name none; it is not a missing classifier masquerading as installed. Would run now describes the actual fallback. Required configured roles, such as embeddings, also require a compatible enabled model; use AI Setup for role and backend selection.

Install / repair explicitly starts a background catalog installer, including missing runtime packages for packaged ONNX models. Import model opens a folder chooser and validates/copies the supported package in a worker; Validate checks an existing installation. Global model operations are serialized, so another installation cannot write into the same assets simultaneously. Download/package installation can be cancelled; folder copy and validation finish their current operation. Closing this panel requests installer cancellation and ignores late UI results. Model assets are global and are shared with AI Setup; source plans are project-specific. Catalog hardware guidance is not a guarantee of performance on your machine. No download occurs merely by opening the panel.

## Media and further work

Index transcript reads an existing transcript with segments; it does not perform speech recognition. Generate the transcript in the source viewer before indexing media. Local source processing does not launch generative analysis. Relation review, migration resolution, event timelines, stronger classifiers and automatic feedback learning are separate planned deliveries.

title: Reviewing knowledge decisions
summary: Confirm connections, merge or split entity mentions, resolve changed-source mappings and safely undo.
body:
# Reviewing connections, entity grouping and changed source spans

Open Intelligence → Review issues for Relation proposals or Review migration conflicts. The same decision panel is used by entity grouping dialogs. Read both source and target records before confirming. A distinct supporting artifact appears in a third pane when present. Jump to source, target or evidence uses the shared recorded-anchor navigator and reports its actual precision. These panes are read-only; classification edits belong in the ordinary artifact editor.

## Review connections

Intelligence → **Review connections…** goes through links between two entities one at a time. You see the sentence with both names in **bold**, the two entities and their types, and why the link was suggested. Choose what the sentence says in **Save as** (Related, Member of / works for, Located in, Family, Allied, Opposes, Created, Governs; plugins can add types) and **Save connection**, or **Reject** if the sentence does not connect them. **Skip** leaves it for later and **Undo** reverses your last save or reject. Keys: Alt+S save, Alt+R reject, Alt+N skip, Alt+U undo, Alt+G go to the sentence. Filter with **Connections** (Named together, Suggested affiliation, Possibly the same entity, saved types) and **Types** (connections involving a person, place, …). Saving as another type keeps the original suggestion, marked corrected, and adds your typed connection on the same sentence. Review connection… in the Entity Network opens the same view for one link.

## Relation proposals

The highlighted line at the top says, in plain words, why the link exists and what confirming it means; links recorded before Entities 4.7 say that their exact reason was not recorded. For entities, each side shows the entity's name, type, other spellings and mention count, plus one example sentence that names it. The queue lists proposals (suggested affiliations, possible duplicates, argument links); “named in the same sentence” observations and document reading links are not queued, and links to dates or measures are skipped. Use **Types** to review only items about people, places or other types.

Each item is an individual assertion with a direction, relation type, evidence, confidence and recorded producer identity. Several assertions may support the same connection; accepting one does not accept the others. Confirm accepts the displayed assertion; Reject rejects it. Missing, rejected or obsolete endpoints/evidence prevent acceptance but still allow rejection. Source-scoped queues include either endpoint and the evidence source. Structural links such as citations and entity mentions use their typed correction tools instead of this default queue. Confidence is a review cue, not a calibrated probability. Acceptance does not train a model or propagate labels.

## Entity grouping

In People & Places or Explore, select two canonical entities of the same category and use Merge selected or Keep separate; the more mentioned entity is kept. Selecting three or more merges them all into the most mentioned one as one decision with one undo; a refusal (different types or a Keep separate rule) changes nothing. Representative occurrence sections show one source example; jump controls use that recorded passage when available. Inspect the direction carefully: mentions of the source entity move into the target across the entire project. The target keeps its name and identity; the old canonical entity becomes superseded with an alias. **Suggested merges** lists entities of the same type whose names look alike (same name, one name inside the other, initials, or close spelling), each with its reason; choosing one fills the target, and nothing merges until you confirm. Pairs marked Keep separate are not suggested. Alternatively choose More → Review entity grouping from an entity/mention inspector, search the target list, and select Merge or Keep separate. Keep separate records a symmetric constraint that blocks merging that pair until undone; it does not train an extractor.

To split, select mentions of one entity and use Split mentions. The complete occurrence browser also offers Split selected mentions on this page, so selection is not limited to the dock's preview. Enter a name and confirm the previewed count. Only explicitly selected occurrences move; choosing the same display name twice creates distinct entities. Selection is scoped to the loaded page. The original words, source spans and extraction identity are unchanged.

Grouping updates canonical parent assignments, per-mention rules and structural mention links. Alias chains and per-mention overrides are reused during later extraction. Unreviewed derived entity relations are retired conservatively and affected entity stages become stale: rerun Entities in Processing to regenerate them. Previously human-reviewed semantic relations are preserved, and may need manual reconsideration if grouping changes their meaning. This is not automatic semantic retargeting of a network.

## Possible duplicate entities

Review issues → **Possible duplicate entities** goes through pairs of same-type entities whose names look alike, best first: the same name (ignoring case, accents and a leading article), one name plus words (“Spain” / “New Spain”, “Lockhart” / “James Lockhart”; only when exactly one longer name contains it, and never a list such as “Cacalchen, Ebtun”), initials (“LAC” / “Latin American Collection”), or a spelling variant within words (“San Cristdébal” / “San Crist6bal”, “Tomas Lépez” / “Tomas Lopez”). The reason shows next to the progress. Save & next merges the less mentioned entity into the other; switch to Keep separate when they are different. Skip and Defer work as in other queues.

## Subgroups and connections instead of merging

Some entities belong under a broader one without being the same: “Yucatec Maya” and “Itza Maya” are Maya groups. Select the broader entity and the ones that belong under it (People & Places or Explore) and use **Group under…**, choosing which one is the umbrella; or in the grouping review choose **Make it a subgroup of the target**. Each stays its own entity with its own type and mentions; the umbrella's row shows “N subgroups (M more mentions)” and expands to each subgroup, which expands to its own mentions. A subgroup shows “Part of” in the inspector and on hover. An entity has one broader entity; a loop (Maya under Yucatec Maya under Maya) is refused. Undo reverses each step.

When two suggested duplicates are different but related (a person and the town named after them), choose **Not the same, but connected: save a connection** and pick the type. They stay separate and are no longer suggested as duplicates. Subgroups and connections can cross types; merging cannot.

## A name that is also a citation

Some names are both an entity and a way of citing a source: “LCN” is an organisation, and every mention of it cites the LCN bibliography entry. Select the entity, choose the entry in **Also cites (bibliography entry)** in Your review (search with Enter) and Save. The entity keeps its type; it is listed as “Organisation + citation”; hovering a mention in the PDF offers the bibliography entry first (Go to opens it), with the entity card as the other choice, and the entry in Citations lists it under **Cited by name** with its mention count. Choose “Not a citation — only a name” to remove the role. The choice is kept when sources are reprocessed.

## Changed-source migration

Migration conflicts indicate that re-extraction could not confidently identify the same observation. Choose a current, unreviewed replacement of the same type and source. Search and page through candidates; a selected target stays available even outside the current search page. Inspect the two spans and their recorded source locations. Tick the explicit correspondence confirmation before confirming. Reviewed semantic fields and explicit citation assignment move to the replacement; its verbatim quote, model identity and machine diagnostics remain its own. The old record remains in history, superseded with an alias. Source jumps through that old reference now follow the confirmed alias to the replacement; cyclic, missing or cross-source/type destinations remain unresolved. A reviewed bibliography entry must be resolved before migrating its citation.

Do not choose a merely similar passage. Reject an obsolete observation or defer when no valid match exists. Ordinary Verify cannot conceal a migration conflict. This workflow maps old and new artifact identities; direct coordinate changes still require the separate confirmed source-location repair dialog.

## Changes, undo and scope

Previews capture a change token and the current project. If a record, mention set, rule, connection or evidence changes before confirmation, reload the preview. Discard decision draft restores the initial choices so you can defer or switch queues without committing. Decisions run in background workers inside database transactions. Undo restores grouping/rules/assertion assessments or migration only when the affected records still match the saved result. It refuses newer conflicting changes. Failed writes roll back together. Reverting a newly split entity retires it rather than deleting its history; a conservative stale-stage marker can remain until recomputation.

The project stores immutable undo snapshots locally; widgets receive opaque receipt IDs. Old pre-journal undo receipts are no longer trusted and require inspecting history. Queue progress and current receipts survive reopening the project. Undo journals are local execution state, not portable pack commands. Source/project clearing closes decision dialogs, cancels pending reads and prevents late writes into another project. A transaction already holding project database locks finishes before a normal project close proceeds.

## More work

This delivery does not add automatic entity-pair proposals, multi-page selection baskets, relation retargeting, model training or validated feedback propagation. Large merges use background transactions but still need broad hardware/memory benchmarking. Model-specific confidence calibration and graph/network views remain separate work.

title: Saved quotes and live artifact references
summary: Read current artifact status, inspect details and jump to recorded source spans without changing historical quotes.
body:
# Saved quotes and live artifact references

Chat citations, RAG context cards, indexed citation search, saved notes and workspace source references reuse the same reference controls. **The saved quoted passage stays unchanged**, even after correction or reprocessing. The status beneath it is checked against the open project in a background task.

- **Unreviewed, verified, corrected or rejected** describe the current artifact assessment; they do not prove the quoted claim is true. Rejected artifacts remain inspectable as historical evidence.
- **Changed since saved** means the artifact revision differs. A current passage that no longer contains the saved quote is labelled separately.
- **Confirmed replacement** follows an explicitly confirmed migration. Inspect opens the replacement while the saved quote remains visible.
- **Stale or superseded** means the recorded processing output needs attention. Unresolved correspondence, missing artifacts, invalid alias chains and removed sources prevent automatic jumping; resolve these in Intelligence → Review issues or Processing.
- **Legacy quote** has no artifact ID. Existing legacy navigation may search text or open a page. Such navigation does not establish an exact recorded anchor.

**Jump to source** uses the shared anchor resolver and reports the precision actually achieved. Page/time/character labels describe recorded coordinates; they are not an exactness guarantee. The source title is backed by source identity; hover for the stored path when titles are identical. **Inspect artifact** opens the shared resizable inspector. Ordinary corrections cannot rewrite source quotes or model identity. Unsaved inspector changes must be saved or discarded before another reference replaces them.

The method line names the recorded producer and actual model, or explicitly says no model was used. Older artifacts with no producer information are labelled as legacy rather than guessing a model. User notes remain commentary separate from source quotes.

Citation search uses indexed citation-bearing passages and ranking scores, not a separate PDF extractor. A relevance score is not a probability. If there are no indexed results, check Citations in Intelligence → Processing. Closing/switching projects disables old reference actions.

Plugins can contribute typed review fields with descriptions and owned help topics through PapyrusAPI; the same question-mark buttons and F1 targets explain those fields. Plugin unload removes their field schema and generated help, while stored artifact content is retained.

## Loading references as you browse

In large projects, saved highlight overlays may take longer to appear the first time while the project prepares them in the background. Your source files are not being changed.

Saved quotes are shown immediately. Their live status, source and method load when the card enters the visible part of a scrolling view. Jump, Inspect and linked-note controls become available after that check. Returning to a recently viewed card can reuse its checked details. Changes to artifacts or sources invalidate those details; hidden cards check again when shown. A pending refresh cannot use an earlier assessment to start an action. Inspect checks the current full artifact before allowing edits. Closing a project clears its live reference details and disables its actions while retaining the historical quote.

## Save commentary

Use Add linked note on eligible source references, or Save linked note on chat/related results. The shared editor saves commentary and a project highlight using a verified source span; it does not modify the source file. See Saving and editing linked project notes for revision guards, original model identity, editing and deletion.

title: Saving and editing linked project notes
summary: Keep source quotations, your commentary and assistant model lineage separate, with verified source spans.
body:
# Linked project notes

Use **Save linked note…** on a chat citation or related result, or **Add linked note…** on an indexed search/RAG/workspace source reference. The same resizable, modeless editor is used everywhere. It previews the saved quote, current artifact status and recorded source span. If a confirmed migration leads to different text, it also displays the current passage being linked.

Write or edit your note, then **Save linked note**. The application validates the project, artifact revision and source file again. If they changed, it refuses the save and keeps your draft: choose **Reload source preview**, inspect the new passage and save again. An unprocessed legacy quote without an artifact ID, unresolved correspondence, rejected/stale artifact, missing file or unverified location must be processed/repaired before saving. Notes and generated interpretations cannot be copied into source-quote artifacts.

## Where the note lives

The note and highlight live in this project. **The original PDF/media/source file is not changed.** A PDF highlight is drawn from the verified recorded geometry when the page is shown; it is not found again by text search. Media notes retain segment-level start/end times, including fractional seconds; word timing is not invented. Project notes are visible in Notes alongside existing physical PDF annotations, and their canonical annotation/note artifacts are available through Intelligence.

The original quotation is immutable in ordinary editing. Your commentary is a separate editable note artifact. **Edit saved note…**, or **Edit note…** in Notes, opens the common artifact inspector. Saving or undoing an edit updates the displayed note body too. Notes color controls affect the project overlay; Delete retires that note/highlight from active retrieval. Source quotes and producer identity are not rewritten. These project highlights are not automatically embedded in an exported PDF; portable project/packs and explicit PDF annotation export still need separate support.

## Who wrote the commentary

Unchanged assistant text records its originating trace/model when that model is unambiguous. The currently selected model is never substituted. If the originating model is absent or ambiguous, model identity is **unknown / model not recorded**, not “no model used.” If you rewrite an assistant suggestion before saving, your note is attributed to you and the original suggestion/model lineage is retained separately. Ordinary later edits retain original producer provenance and record a human revision in history.

## Closing or switching projects

Before a save starts, closing the editor cancels its readers. Once a confirmed atomic save has started, closing the editor does not undo it; it finishes against that project, and late results cannot populate the next project. Repeated delivery of the same save request does not create duplicates. A failed save cannot leave a half-written highlight without its artifacts. Inspect saved notes in Notes to confirm an accepted save after closing the editor.

Press F1 here for this guide. Source-reference controls have their own guide explaining navigation precision and migration. Linked notes preserve the saved span: if the file changes, repair the original source artifact and save a replacement linked note. Ordinary coordinate repair does not rewrite a linked note’s saved anchor.

## Notes from a manual selection

Selecting PDF words, transcript text, reflowable text or an image OCR block opens the same resizable project-note editor. Nothing is saved until you confirm. The editor checks the selected source and location again before saving. PDF highlights use consecutive selected source words and preserve the selected color. Transcript selections keep their selected segments even when playback is elsewhere, exclude displayed timestamp labels, and preserve fractional times. Transcript timing is segment-level: it does not establish exact spoken-word timing or guarantee transcription accuracy.

A manual selection does not pretend to have an earlier artifact ID. Saving creates its own annotation and commentary artifacts and records the selection method, source hash, geometry or segment window. A transcript's producing model is retained as input provenance; selecting or commenting on it is a human action, so that annotation correctly says no model produced the selection. If the file or transcript changes while the editor is open, save is refused until you review the updated selection.

## Managing a linked note from the workspace

The workspace's source-highlight deletion action opens Manage linked project note for project-owned linked notes. Inspect the original quote and saved commentary, use Edit note to open the shared inspector, change the highlight color or explicitly delete the project note. Reload after another edit before retrying a stale action. Deletion retires the project note and removes its overlay. Workspace cards keep their own text and can be removed separately. Workspace-only text/color changes do not overwrite reviewed canonical commentary. Importing an analysis graph no longer creates physical annotations in source PDFs.

## Text and image selections

Text selections preserve the exact extracted block and raw character range. Literal markup, emoji and repeated text keep their own occurrence; the source search bar is not used to find a replacement. Image selections use the recorded OCR block's pixel rectangle. This covers the OCR block, not individual words or proof that OCR is correct. The selected quote is read only and scrollable; your separate commentary is editable.

The viewer reads already extracted blocks in a worker. If extraction predates source fingerprints or the file has changed, open Intelligence → Processing, explicitly rerun Parsed blocks/source extraction, then reopen the source. Merely opening a note will not download/run an OCR model. Source Jump opens the recorded text/image viewer, including when book mode was selected. If those recorded blocks no longer exist, the location cannot be silently replaced by similar text.

## Adopting an existing PDF annotation

In Notes, **Adopt as project note…** previews an on-disk PDF text highlight and its existing commentary in the shared editor. Confirm Save linked note to create a project copy; no write occurs when merely browsing or previewing. Its original physical annotation remains in the PDF, so both observations can appear in Notes. Refresh Notes after saving physical annotations in the source viewer: unsaved physical annotations are not read from another thread's mutable PDF handle.

The preview checks page/object identity, annotation content/geometry and source bytes again at save. If something changes, refresh Notes and review a fresh preview. Re-adoption preserves an existing project copy and its later edits: use Edit saved note to change that copy. Old `AINote` titles do not establish model authorship; unchanged imported commentary says original authorship is unrecorded. Editing that commentary during adoption records your new commentary while retaining the original input separately. Nontext or disconnected highlights that cannot be verified require selecting a new passage.

Physical annotation edits elsewhere, source-file export, book-view selections, other-format acceptance and full history/Notes virtualization remain separate work. New unguarded PDF, raw rendered-offset/image-locator and filename/quote-search save requests are rejected; plugins should use prepare_reference_note/save_reference_note, or prepare_selection_note/save_selection_note with the returned project/token guards.


## Browse every note

Choose Current Document or Entire Project and browse Previous/Next pages. Notes loads only while visible. Use Refresh notes after changing an on-disk file. The tag selector suggests a bounded list; type any exact tag name and press Enter to filter by other tags. A page can contain no matches while Next still leads to more sources. Missing or unreadable physical PDFs appear as diagnostics without hiding project notes. The selected bubble previews long quotes/commentary; open the shared inspector or source to read the full saved content.

## Existing source annotations

Legacy physical annotation edit, recolor and delete controls are read-only. Adopt a supported physical PDF highlight as a project note, or select its passage again. This keeps the original PDF unchanged and records unknown legacy authorship honestly. A legacy AINote title does not establish which model or person wrote it.

## Independent workspace copies

Workspace cards keep their saved commentary and color when the canonical note changes or is deleted. Manage source note / refresh workspace copy opens the project-note manager with the current canvas copy alongside it. The explicit replacement action changes that one card only, with undo. If the note or card changed since preview, close and review again. Managing multiple selected notes uses Previous selected note / Next selected note in one window; deletion still requires reviewing an individual note.

title: Contextual event timelines and personal filters
summary: Browse date-linked event candidates, combine entity identities with Boolean filters, and save personal research views.
body:
# Contextual event timelines

The Timeline displays a chronological rail of event candidates built from stored date artifacts and their recorded sentence or transcript evidence. It does not rerun extraction, download a model, call generative AI or assert that an event really happened. Select a row to inspect the canonical date and use Jump to source for its recorded location. Verify date and Reject date affect that date artifact; Hide selected events affects only your personal view.

## Filters and entity identities

Expand **Filters & saved views**. Enter `Alice AND ("Bob Smith" OR Carol)` or use **Find entity**, choose a typed identity and **Add entity**. Previous/Next below the entity selector reaches further matches. AND requires both entities in the same evidence window; OR requires either; NOT excludes a co-mention in that window. NOT is not proof that a person had no real-world connection to an event. Multiword names need double quotes. Unknown or ambiguous names are rejected; select a typed identity instead. Added choices and saved expressions bind to canonical IDs, not a guess from their displayed names. Apply filters runs the query; invalid dates or expressions leave the previous results visible with an explanation.

## Sentence and proximity rules

**Same recorded sentence** uses current entity mentions attached to the uniquely containing source sentence or transcript segment. This is co-mention, not a participant role or semantic relationship. **Words from date, within its sentence** also requires validated raw/sentence coordinate mapping, and counts whitespace-separated words containing letters/numbers between the date and entity; punctuation alone is not counted. A zero-word window means adjacent or overlapping spans. Soft hyphens use the existing source normalization map. Unknown, ambiguous, invalid, oversized or multiblock coordinate mappings abstain; they cannot falsely satisfy NOT. Raw/normalized word maps are bounded to 32,000 context characters; use Same recorded sentence for larger contexts or process finer source segments. A dense batch can exceed the bounded mention budget: diagnostics explain incomplete matches and recommend narrowing the source/date scope.

## Calendar intervals and uncertainty

From and Through accept YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Both ends are inclusive. A year means its whole calendar year, a month its whole calendar month: an event dated only 2018 can overlap a June 2018 filter without claiming an exact day. Unresolved dates appear only when Include unresolved dates is enabled and no calendar bounds are set. No undated rows are fabricated from claims. Certainty and precision retain their recorded values; unrecorded is not a probability.

## Excluded dates and old artifacts

Default candidates require an explicitly eligible current date and readable context. Citation/reference, bibliography, publication, copyright and metadata dates stay out. **All date observations (diagnostic)** shows excluded observations with reasons and still respects the other filters. Older artifacts without recorded eligibility need Dates processing again or diagnostic inspection; browsing never starts that processing automatically.

## Saved filters and personal exclusions

Hide selected events excludes those date IDs from the working research view without rejecting or editing artifacts. Show hidden events lets you select and restore them. Give the filters a name and Save to retain the expression, identity bindings, interval rules and exclusions in this project. Choose a saved definition and Load to apply it. Source scope and general search stay separate unless you enable **Save source scope and search with this perspective**. Loading that definition restores the recorded source ID and text; missing sources are reported without substituting the whole project. New / reset starts clean working filters without deleting saved definitions; Remove saved filters removes the selected definition while keeping the current working filters.

Saved definitions use project/revision guards. Another editor's update refuses a stale overwrite and retains your draft; Load the current definition before overwriting it. These project-local IDs are not yet a portable pack format. Hide/exclude IDs do not automatically migrate to unrelated replacement artifacts. ## Source-backed manual events and candidate decisions

In Artifacts select a sentence/transcript segment, or select a contextual Timeline row, then **Create event from passage**. The shared source preview verifies its exact location and source hash before saving. Enter your own event summary and interpreted date/optional end; the original quotation stays unchanged. This creates a canonical human-authored interpretation, not a new extracted source quotation. A missing/changed file or stale preview refuses the save. Model is explicitly none. Open **Edit event / participants** to revise a candidate, its summary, certainty or interval, and assign typed roles to recorded co-mentions. Candidate, accepted and dismissed are event decisions; Verify date checks the date observation separately. A user-accepted event can override an erroneous automated date exclusion; dismissal removes it from the default view but keeps it in diagnostics and history. Undo event edits through the existing guarded artifact review/history controls. Creation itself is retained as a canonical record; reject an unwanted authored event.

## Participants and same-event filters

Same sentence means recorded co-mention, not participation. **Assigned roles on accepted event** restricts Boolean matches to your explicitly assigned participant/organizer/subject/location/witness roles in that event. NOT means no assigned role in this saved interpretation, not a real-world absence. Unaccepted or incomplete contexts cannot prove NOT. Role choices are limited to current recorded co-mentions, with at most 32 editable choices per preview. A manual date need not occur literally in its quotation, so word proximity for manual interpretations abstains rather than inventing a date position.

## Calendar chart and personal inclusions

The chart shows proportional intervals for this result page. Use Calendar zoom and Apply, then scroll; click an interval to inspect the matching table record. Hatching denotes certainty other than confirmed, not a probability. The table provides the same evidence for keyboard/assistive use. A YYYY/month date occupies its whole possible interval. The optional authored end date permits explicit ranges; inclusive filters match interval overlap. Diagnostic observations may be personally included without relabelling them as verified events; Save retains inclusions/exclusions and zoom. Check replaced event IDs reports confirmed same-source correspondence and unresolved IDs; Apply confirmed replacements is an explicit decision, followed by Save. Unknown IDs are retained, never guessed from text.

See Entity Networks for independent evidence-backed connections. Native screen-reader and physical-hardware acceptance remain release checks.

title: Entity networks
summary: Explore current evidence-backed connections independently of argument maps.
body:
# Entity networks

Open Intelligence → Entity Network. The table pages current assertions whose two endpoints are canonical entities and whose evidence is current and in the selected source scope. Source scope and general search filter the evidence, not global entity names. Rejected, stale, missing-evidence and obsolete argument assessments do not establish visible connections.

## What a line means

Co-occurrence observation: entities share recorded evidence; it never becomes a semantic relationship just because its assertion was verified. Candidate relationship: an unreviewed semantic assertion, or an explicitly candidate-type assertion, remains a proposal. Accepted relationship: a verified/corrected semantic assertion with current source evidence. Dashed lines are observations/candidates; solid lines are accepted semantic links. Only directed relationships have arrowheads. Confidence is the originating score, not a calibrated probability. No new relationship is inferred or saved by browsing.

## Explore and review

Select a connection to see its reason and source passage. Jump to source uses the evidence artifact's recorded span. Expand source/target entity or click an entity in the diagram to explore one hop; All entities clears the focus. Review connection opens the same guarded relation decision panel as other intelligence surfaces, including evidence, verification/rejection and undo. The diagram shows at most 40 entities from this page; the table and Previous/Next expose all connections. Its deterministic circular placement does not imply semantic distance, community or importance.

## Personal perspectives

Expand Saved network perspectives. Save a focus entity, candidate visibility and personal hidden-assertion IDs; optionally include source scope/search. Hide selected changes your perspective only; Restore hidden connections clears personal exclusions. Load is explicit. Store tokens protect against stale overwrites. Definitions are project-local; portable pack ID remapping remains a release task. Keyboard users can use the table and Expand buttons for everything the diagram supports.

title: Workspace Inbox
summary: Page project notes, canonical entities and legacy discovery observations.
body:
# Workspace Inbox

Open Workspace → Inbox. Choose project notes/read-only source observations, canonical intelligence entities or explicitly saved legacy discovery entities. Each worker request returns at most 25 records; Previous/Next covers the collection, including empty selective pages with continuation. Current canvas IDs are excluded. Opening/restoring a workspace never starts a source scan; explicit Inbox browsing reads only bounded PDF annotation pages off the GUI thread.

## Independent copies

Select one or more rows on the current page, inspect their quotation/commentary, then Add selected. The worker rechecks project/revisions and physical-observation fingerprints; changing the project or workspace refuses stale application. Copies preserve the existing note or legacy entity import behavior. Editing a canvas copy does not silently change canonical notes/entities or source files. Use Notes/Artifact Inspector for guarded canonical edits; the original PDF annotation remains read only and can be explicitly adopted through Notes.

Canonical entities keep their artifact reference; old saved discoveries keep their original ontology type and properties. Source-less canonical entity references remain entities, not fabricated source quotations. Empty results may mean all matching records are already on this canvas. Refresh restarts after changes. Native desktop and very large workspace/import timing remain release checks.

## Stored legacy snapshots

A separate collection preserves DB-only legacy note records that no longer have a physical annotation. These are explicitly unverified stored snapshots and may differ from the current source. Importing one copies its saved quotation/commentary; it does not assert that the original annotation still exists or change the source file.

title: Event summary
summary: Typed event interpretation field.
body:
# Event summary

A human-authored description of an event candidate. It is stored separately from the verbatim source quotation; editing it never rewrites evidence. Maximum 4000 characters.

title: Event interval end
summary: Typed event interpretation field.
body:
# Event interval end

An optional inclusive end using YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Year/month ends occupy the full final calendar interval. The end must not precede the interpreted start. Blank means the start date’s own precision interval.

title: Event candidate decision
summary: Typed event interpretation field.
body:
# Event candidate decision

Candidate means an observation awaiting event review. Accepted is your explicit interpretation of an event and can override automated exclusion. Dismissed excludes it from default timelines while retaining source evidence/history. This is separate from Verify date, which reviews the date observation.

title: Event participant roles
summary: Typed event interpretation field.
body:
# Event participant roles

Assign co-mentioned, participant, organizer, subject, location or witness to entities already recorded in this source sentence/segment. Co-mentioned is the default observation and claims no semantic relationship. Other roles are your explicit interpretation, not model inference. Same-event Boolean filters use assigned roles only on accepted events; unavailable/dense mappings cannot prove absence.

title: Memory Manager
summary: See what is using memory, unload models, and let Papyrus keep enough memory free automatically.
body:
# Memory manager

Papyrus keeps one record of everything that holds a lot of memory — AI models loaded in Ollama or llama.cpp, the spaCy language model, local ONNX models, the PDF viewer's rendered pages, open PDFs, extraction caches and background workers (OCR, speech-to-text) — and manages it in one place.

Open it from **Settings → 🧠 Memory**, from the **process monitor** button on the toolbar (**Open memory panel**), or with the *Memory Panel* shortcut (bind it in Settings → Shortcuts).

## The chart

The donut adds up to your total RAM:

- **Each loaded model** (for example a chat model in Ollama) is its own slice.
- **Papyrus app** — everything inside Papyrus itself, including spaCy and caches.
- **Background workers** — helper processes such as Tesseract OCR.
- **Other apps** — the rest of your system.
- **Free** — available memory.

**Memory pressure** is *Normal*, *Elevated* (free memory is getting close to the reserve) or *Critical* (below the reserve).

## Manual control

- **Unload all models** — frees every model Papyrus loaded. They load again the next time they are needed.
- **Free caches now** — drops caches that rebuild quickly (viewer pages, extraction cache, extra open PDFs).
- Select a row in **Loaded components** and choose **Unload** or **Trim**.

Models loaded by other apps are shown but never unloaded automatically.

## Automatic management

- **Memory reserve** — the share of RAM kept free (default 15%). When free memory falls below it, idle caches are trimmed first, then idle local models, then the embedding model, then an idle chat model. Anything in use is never unloaded.
- **Idle limits** — a chat model unloads after 10 idle minutes and the embedding model after 3 (Ollama is told the same limit).
- **Preload at startup** — *When memory allows* (default) skips warming a model that would not fit; it loads when you first use it. The log says why.
- **Before heavy work** — OCR, transcription, embeddings and intelligence stages ask for memory first; idle models are released so the work does not push the computer into swap, and OCR uses as many parallel pages as fit.
- **Background workers** — *Automatic* sizes parallel work to free memory.
- **Hold new background jobs while memory is critical** — queued background jobs wait (shown as *Waiting for memory* in the process monitor, with **Run anyway**) and start when memory recovers, or after two minutes.
- **Mode** — *Balanced*, *Aggressive* (keeps 5% more free) or *Off* (monitor only).

Environment variables such as `PAPYRUS_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` still override these settings; the panel says when one is set.

## Freezes

If the window stops responding for more than a quarter of a second, Papyrus records what it was doing in `stall.log` in its data folder. Long freezes are written while they are still happening, so the log survives a forced quit.

title: Notes, references and contents links
summary: Preview a linked passage, jump to it and return to reading.
body:
# Reading links

Run Sentences & sections and Citations for a source. Hover over a dotted link to preview its note, bibliography entry or chapter heading. Click the link or Go to to jump to the exact passage. A grouped citation offers a destination selector so you can preview and jump to each cited reference. Alt+Left returns to the previous reading position. Open in Intelligence opens the target for inspection. Preview reading link is available through the shortcut registry.

Settings → Reading controls smart links. Native PDF links also work before extraction. A missing or ambiguous target is left unresolved; OCR can lose note markers, so not every printed marker will become a link.

The Intelligence overview separates current entities, mentions, notes, references, contents entries and argument units. Processing details shows observation totals and extraction history; these totals are not counts of unique entities. Intelligence → Notes shows document notes and markers. Citations shows references and their citations. Contents shows headings and contents entries. People & Places groups linked entity mentions. Source quotes stay separate from editable review fields; Details contains provenance.

title: Optional entity resources (AI Setup)
summary: Four optional local resources can improve how names are found and typed: a multilingual recogniser, a place gazetteer, a language identifier and a sentence encoder.
body:
Install them in AI Setup (or from the Entities stage details). Each is off until you tick “Use in this project's entity extraction” on its card; ticking it re-runs Entities for your sources.

• Multilingual entity recogniser (GLiNER): reads names in context in any language and votes on their type, including technical terms (methods, datasets, conditions, organisms). It is a second opinion: how the document uses a name (“in Tekanto”, “Maya women”, “Landa wrote”) still decides first. Its labels are editable in entity_labels.json in the model folder.
• Place-name gazetteer (GeoNames, CC BY 4.0): supports typing a name as a place only when the document also uses it like one, after “in/near/from” or among other places of the same region. A name in the list is never a place on that alone.
• Language identifier (GlotLID): recognises the language of each passage so the English name model is not trusted on Hawaiian, Latin, Spanish or other text.
• Sentence encoder (bge-small): features for argument-role labelling; used once a trained role head is available.

Every vote is stored on the mention with its reason, so you can see why a name got its type. All resources run locally and are released from memory when idle (Settings → Memory).

title: Cross-references and note markers in scans
summary: “See Table 7.2”, “Chapter 5”, “Appendix B” and “note 12” link to what they name; note numbers a scan's OCR misread are re-read from the page image.
body:
After processing, hovering a reference such as “see Table 7.2”, “Chapter 5”, “Appendix B”, “§ 4” or “supra note 12” shows the caption, heading or note it names, with Go to and Back. A reference links only when the document has exactly one matching target; references to other works (“Roys 1939: part 2”) and ambiguous ones are left unlinked rather than guessed.

In scanned books the OCR text often turns small raised note numbers into marks such as ’ ” ° *. When Tesseract is installed (AI Setup → OCR engine), Papyrus re-reads those marks from the page image, digits only, and accepts a number only when it names an existing, unclaimed note of that chapter and keeps the chapter's markers in order. Markers it cannot read with confidence are left unlinked and recorded for review; numbers are never guessed from the sequence.

title: Entity links while reading
summary: Hover a name in a PDF to see its entity; Alt+] and Alt+[ step through its mentions.
body:
Turn on “Show entity links” in Settings → Reading (or with the Show entity links action). Names that the Entities stage found are then underlined with a dashed line. Hover one to see its card: the entity's name and type, other spellings, which mention this is out of how many in the document, how many mentions and sources it has across the project, and why it was recognised (for example, matched from a name found elsewhere, or typed from how the document uses it).

Go to jumps to the next mention of the same entity in this document, wrapping to the first; Alt+] and Alt+[ jump to the next and previous mention of the entity you last hovered, and keep walking from where you arrive. Alt+Left returns to where you were. Open in Intelligence opens the entity itself.

Only mentions whose exact position on the page is known are shown, so underlines always sit on the name. Run Entities first; the setting is off by default.

title: Organize and auto-tag sources
summary: Group sources into tag folders, apply deterministic rules, or tag a whole import.
body:
# Source tags

In Document Explorer, turn on **Tags as folders** to replace the flat list with collapsible tag categories. Folder icons use each tag's color. In Tag Manager, select a tag and set **Nested under** to define an explicit parent; for example, put Treaties under Law. Explicit parents work even when both tags have exactly the same sources. Where no parent is set, Papyrus may infer a safe parent from strict source-set containment. A source with both tags appears only in its deepest applicable folder, while sources with no tags appear under **Untagged**.

In Tag Manager, select a tag and choose **Auto-tag Sources**. Pick a source field and rule, preview every match, then apply. Rules inspect saved source metadata only; they do not read document contents or call a model. Regular expressions are available for advanced filename and path matching.

When adding sources, expand **Add with tags** and select one or more existing tags. You can create and select a new tag without leaving the dialog. Every source successfully added in that batch receives all selected tags.
